question: Are 1400-char chunks too coarse for gemma; do halves or sentences fix the top-1 losses?

method.halves: chunk body split at the sentence boundary (. ! ? + whitespace) nearest the character midpoint; each half >= 20% of the body, else the chunk stays one unit (31/16/1 chunks in fde/aieng/novel)
method.sentences: answer._sentences(body), keep sentences with >= 12 words, accumulate in order while the running character count stays within the parent's own length; no cap ever bound (0 dropped); chunks with no qualifying sentence fall back to the whole body (28/9/2 chunks)
method.formatting: documents use retrieve.format_input(model,'document', unit_text, heading) i.e. 'title: <heading> | text: <unit>' - exactly the engine's document formatting; queries use the engine's 'task: search result | query: ' prefix
method.ranking: cosine(unit, query); parent score = max unit score; parents ranked descending; metrics at parent level
method.no_writes: data/ untouched; vectors held in /tmp/Granularity and the engine imported read-only

baseline_reproduction.note: matches PROTOCOL 19/35 and 30/35 exactly; Dims and DualFusion independently report the same 19 top-1 and 30 top-5 over the same 35 rows

cost.ollama: shared with three other experiments; 30-35 ms/unit measured under contention, 24 ms/unit for a quiet 64-text batch before the others ramped up

diagnostics.note: no short-text score inflation (per-query Pearson r between unit length and cosine is 0.00-0.14, not negative); mean pooling is worse than max everywhere, so the sentence-level loss is granularity, not an aggregation artefact

truncation_256d.method: prefix truncation of the stored whole-chunk and unit vectors to the first 256 dims, query re-normalized; no re-embedding
truncation_256d.correction: first pass of this table truncated but did not re-normalize each stored vector; prefix norms vary 0.66-0.72 so that biased the ordering. Numbers below re-normalize every truncated vector (full 768-d vectors are unit norm, so all 768-d results are unaffected). They now match Dims per row: 21/32 on the 35 rows.
truncation_256d.note: halves+256 is the highest point estimate (23 top-1) but adds nothing reliable over whole-256: +2 top-1 (CI -5..+9) and -2 top-5 (CI -7..+3) for 9.5 MB of vectors against 4.9 MB. Truncation alone is the tighter result: whole-256 vs whole-768 is +2 top-1 (CI 0..+5) and +2 top-5 (0..+5).

all_35.sentences: not extended: ruled out on the 20-row subset by top-5 (-4, CI -9..0) and 6x index
